episode_title: Luxury Tennis Vacations That Turn Strangers Into Friends | Troy Manditch

real_qa.q: What pricing range does Lux Group of Editors offer for tennis and paddle travel experiences?
real_qa.r: Troy explains that Lux Group of Editors pricing varies widely depending on the trip format. Set trips typically range from $2,000 to $8,000 per person in the mid four-figures range. Private group trips can range from $2,500 to $10,000 or $20,000 per person, with no set limit on what he will arrange. The goal is to deliver exceptional experiences under $10,000 where guests have high-quality activities like Michelin-star meals, tennis clubs, and guided tours rather than expensive hotel stays.
real_qa.requete: Lux Group of Editors tennis trip pricing cost

real_qa.q: How does Lux Group of Editors curate luxury tennis vacations to ensure exceptional guest experiences?
real_qa.r: Troy describes an extensive scouting process where he researches destinations thoroughly, considers multiple venue options, and narrows selections based on beauty, value, food quality, local people, and long-term guest satisfaction. His goal is to have guests arrive with minimal effort required—everything is pre-arranged with vendors and partners executing their roles perfectly so guests can simply show up and enjoy. He invests countless hours in manual work including destination research, scouting trips to evaluate tennis clubs, Michelin-star restaurants, tour guides, and activities to ensure every detail works seamlessly.
real_qa.requete: how Lux Group curates luxury tennis vacations

real_qa.q: What was Troy Manditch's background before founding Lux Group of Editors?
real_qa.r: Troy was a tennis coach for 10 years and founded Miami Dinner Club at age 22 after moving to Miami without knowing anyone. Miami Dinner Club was a private members club connecting people aged 30 and above who were honest, intellectually curious, and passionate. Members could show up solo to curated weekly events at restaurants, private chefs venues, and activities like paddle, pickleball, and kayaking, then leave with new friendships. The business succeeded at making friendships but became unsustainable because Troy had to be physically present every week.
real_qa.requete: Troy Manditch Miami Dinner Club background

real_qa.q: Why did Troy Manditch transition from Miami Dinner Club to luxury travel experiences?
real_qa.r: Troy explains that Miami Dinner Club failed as a business model because it was too successful at making friendships—once people made connections, they no longer needed the service, making it unsustainable income. With travel trips, he can take clients repeatedly to different destinations across Costa Rica, Majorca, Brazil, South of France, and Sardinia over multiple years, creating ongoing revenue. He also transitioned because he is more passionate about travel than networking dinners, and the travel business allows him to combine his passion for visiting new countries with his professional work.
real_qa.requete: why Troy Manditch switched from dinners to travel trips

real_qa.q: How does human connection factor into Lux Group of Editors luxury travel philosophy?
real_qa.r: Troy emphasizes that meeting amazing people and developing connections through shared interests is the most important aspect of his trips, beyond just having a great vacation. He notes that science consistently shows quality of human connections is the most valuable indicator of health, longevity, and enjoyment. He deliberately curates experiences around shared passions—particularly tennis and paddle sports—because athletes in these communities are typically kind, interesting, and create lasting friendships. His trips are designed so guests show up with a good attitude and leave having formed genuine human bonds with like-minded travelers.
real_qa.requete: Lux Group human connection travel experiences

guest.bio_context: Troy Manditch is a tennis coach with 10 years of experience whose parents introduced him to tennis and racquet sports. He previously founded Miami Dinner Club at age 22, a private members club in Miami connecting intellectually curious people through curated dinners and events. He has since transitioned to building luxury travel experiences centered on tennis and paddle, having visited approximately 30 countries and aiming to visit three new countries every year for 50 years.
